Good locations become more valuable with time. Cities 
grow around them, customer catchments deepen and 
new opportunities emerge. At Phoenix, we have built our 
business around this principle. We invest in locations with 
enduring potential, build destinations that remain relevant 
and continue improving them long after they open.
At Phoenix, 
value is not 
created in 
bursts but 
accumulated, 
and then it 
compounds.
Compounding comes from reinvesting 
in what we already own. Existing 
destinations are refreshed, repositioned 
and densified, while new uses such as 
offices and hospitality are added where 
they strengthen the destination.
As our destinations mature, they create 
opportunities that were not fully visible at 
inception, allowing us to unlock greater 
value from the same location over time.
Our capabilities compound as well. 
Retailer relationships deepen, operating 
knowledge improves and each new 
development benefits from the experience 
gained across the portfolio. The cash 
generated by mature assets is reinvested 
into enhancing existing destinations and funding the next phase of growth, 
supported by prudent capital allocation. 
This creates a self-reinforcing cycle of 
growth and value creation.
The outcome is visible over time. 
From FY06 to FY26, EBITDA increased 
from approximately H26 crore to 
H2,637 crore, representing a CAGR of 
approximately 26% through multiple 
economic and market cycles.
Built to Compound describes both 
how we have grown and how we 
intend to create value from here: by 
strengthening existing destinations, 
building on the capabilities developed 
over time and investing with a long-
term perspective.Built to 
Compound

About us 
BUILDING INDIA’S 
MOST LOVED 
DESTINATIONS
We are one of India’s leading 
owners, operators and 
developers of retail led mixed-
use destinations, with a portfolio 
spanning over 20 million sq. ft. 
across retail, offices, hospitality 
and residential developments. 
Our growth has been guided by deliberate 
geographic choices rather than opportunistic 
expansion. Over the past two decades, we 
have established a presence across 14 cities 
(covering operational and under construction 
assets) in India, selecting markets where an 
integrated destination could meaningfully shape 
how people shop, work, stay and spend their 
time, not merely add another address to the map.
What began with retail has evolved into a 
broader retail-led mixed-use destination 
platform with offices, hotels and premium 
residences adding depth and diversity to our 
development. Together, these assets create 
integrated environments where consumption, 
commerce, hospitality and community come 
together, generating enduring value for 
consumers, occupiers, residents and the cities 
we serve.
Our capabilities span the entire real estate value 
chain, including planning, execution, marketing, 
management, maintenance and sales, giving us 
control not only over what we build, but how it 
performs over time. This integrated approach is 
what sets a Phoenix destination apart: it is not 
just a place people visit, but a place they return 
to, again and again.

Dear Shareholders,
Over the last two decades, we have operated through 
several economic cycles, periods of market disruption and, 
more recently, heightened geopolitical and macroeconomic 
uncertainty. Through each of these periods, our approach 
has remained consistent: stay focused on what we can 
control, operate our assets well, execute our development 
plans with discipline and invest for the long term.
From FY06 to FY26, our EBITDA has grown at a CAGR of 
approximately 26%. FY26 was another strong example of 
this resilience and consistency. Consolidated revenue grew 
by 16% to H4,423 crore, EBITDA increased by 22% to H2,637 
crore and operating free cash flow increased by 23% to 
H2,140 crore, even as we continued to invest across our 
existing assets and development pipeline.It is against this backdrop that we chose this 
year's theme, ‘Built to Compound’.
For us, compounding is not only about financial growth. It 
comes from making our existing assets more productive, 
reinvesting in them as their markets evolve, adding 
new uses and income streams and deploying the cash 
generated by the business into the next phase of growth.
Our experience over the last two decades has reinforced 
a simple belief: great destinations create durable value. 
When retail, hospitality, offices, entertainment and 
community experiences come together in a destination that 
remains relevant to its market, the asset can continue to 
grow and compound over decades.Chairman's Letter to 
Shareholders

only about financial growth. 
It comes from making

productive, reinvesting in

adding new uses and income 
streams and deploying 
the cash generated by the 
business into the next phase 
of growth.

ATUL RUIA  
ChairmanFY26: A Strong Year Across Our Businesses
FY26 saw progress across each of our businesses: retail 
consumption reached a new high, our recently completed 
offices continued to lease up, hospitality delivered another 
strong year and residential bookings more than doubled.
At the same time, we continued to invest in our existing 
assets and development pipeline, completed first tranche 
payment to CPP Investments in the ISMDPL transaction and 
maintained balance-sheet discipline. I highlight below some 
of the developments that stood out during the year. Shishir's 
letter that follows provides a detailed discussion of the 
performance of our businesses and their operating drivers.
Retail
Retail remains the foundation of our platform. Consumption 
across our portfolio reached a record H16,587 crore in 
FY26, an increase of 21% over the previous year.
A defining feature of our retail business is our ability to 
continue creating value from established destinations. 
During FY26, this was particularly visible at Pune and 
Bengaluru.
At Phoenix Avenue of Stars, Pune (earlier known as 
Phoenix MarketCity Pune), EBITDA had already grown 
more than fourfold from FY13 to FY26. Despite this strong 
performance, we chose to accept a period of disruption and 
lower trading occupancy to comprehensively transform the 
destination for its next phase of growth.
We upgraded the facade and arrival experience, premiumised 
the brand mix, introduced new flagship formats and created 
a new identity for the destination. In May 2026, Phoenix 
MarketCity Pune was relaunched as Phoenix Avenue of Stars. 
At Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore, we similarly upgraded 
parts of the existing retail offering as the destination evolves 
into a much larger mixed-use campus.
The early results are encouraging. In Q1 FY27, 
consumption and trading density at Phoenix Avenue 
of Stars grew by 29% and 26%, respectively. Phoenix 
MarketCity Bangalore recorded consumption growth of 
22% and trading density growth of 15%.
Offices
Over the last two years, our completed office portfolio 
has more than doubled to approximately 4.8 million sq. 
ft. During FY26, we leased approximately 2.2 million sq. 
ft. across the portfolio and ended the year with leased 
occupancy of 70%.
The next phase is to convert this leasing momentum into 
occupancy and income. In Q1 FY27, office income grew 
by 44% over the previous year as tenants moved into the 
recently completed assets.We have also been deliberate about the product we 
are creating. Our offices are designed as amenity-
led workplaces within larger mixed-use destinations, 
combining Grade-A workspaces with access to retail, 
dining and leisure and hospitality-grade amenities. As 
the recently completed portfolio stabilises, offices should 
become a materially larger second annuity business for 
Phoenix.
Hospitality
Our hospitality portfolio delivered another strong year, 
with EBITDA increasing by 14% to H276 crore.
The St. Regis, Mumbai, continued to lead the portfolio 
and remains an important part of the Phoenix Palladium 
destination. Its performance demonstrates the value a 
high-quality hotel can create both as a standalone business 
and as part of a larger mixed-use ecosystem. We are taking 
this model forward at Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore, 
where the Grand Hyatt Bangalore is under construction as 
part of the expanded campus.
 
Residential
Residential bookings more than doubled to H471 crore in 
FY26. We continue to approach this business selectively, 
focusing on locations where we see a strong underlying 
market, a differentiated product opportunity and the 
potential to create meaningful value.
As we progressively monetise the remaining ready 
inventory at One Bangalore West and Kessaku, we are 
preparing the next phase of growth. Towers 8 and 9 at 
One Bangalore West, comprising approximately 0.66 
million sq. ft. of saleable area, and One Belvedere in 
Kolkata, comprising approximately 1 million sq. ft., are 
both nearing launch as we finalise design and secure the 
remaining approvals.
Our Vision for 2030
Our growth through 2030 is increasingly visible within the 
portfolio we already own and the development pipeline 
already under our control.
It will come from four principal sources: continued growth 
from our existing retail destinations; the stabilisation 
of our recently completed office portfolio; new retail-
led mixed-use developments in Kolkata, Surat, Thane, 
Coimbatore and Chandigarh; and further densification 
of our established campuses at Lower Parel and Phoenix 
MarketCity Bangalore.
A significant part of this programme is already under 
execution.

Lower Parel: Building on Phoenix Palladium
Lower Parel remains one of the clearest examples of 
how we have created value by continuing to build on a 
successful destination. High Street Phoenix evolved into 
Phoenix Palladium and was subsequently complemented 
by The St. Regis, Mumbai. EBITDA from the overall complex 
has grown close to four times between FY13 and FY26.
We are now entering the next phase, with over 2 million 
sq. ft. of additional leasable area scheduled for completion 
over the next two years: approximately 0.5 million sq. ft. of 
retail in 2027 and approximately 1.6 million sq. ft. of offices 
in 2028. Together, these additions will further integrate 
retail, offices, hospitality, dining and social experiences 
within the precinct.
Beyond this, we are advancing design development and 
have secured key approvals for approximately 1.5 million 
sq. ft. of additional development potential acquired in 
March 2025. Our focus is on identifying the use that can 
create the greatest long-term value from this opportunity.
Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore: Making of an Icon
At Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore, we are building on the 
strength of an established retail destination to create a 
much larger integrated mixed-use campus.
Phase II, comprising additional retail, Art Exchange offices 
and the Grand Hyatt Bangalore, is nearing delivery and is 
targeted for completion in 2027. At the same time, Phase III 
is commencing construction, adding the next layer of retail, 
offices and hospitality.
Taken together, these phases will transform our Whitefield 
campus from an approximately 1 million sq. ft. retail 
destination today into an over 4 million sq. ft. integrated 
mixed-use campus.
The Pipeline Ahead
Our new retail destinations in Kolkata and Surat, each of 
approximately 1 million sq. ft., are targeted for completion 
in 2027 and have achieved strong leasing progress ahead 
of completion. Thane, Coimbatore and Chandigarh have also 
progressed from planning and approvals into execution, with 
destination retail forming the anchor for each development. 
Our next residential projects in Bengaluru and Kolkata add 
another component to this pipeline.
By 2030, we expect Phoenix to have more than 18 million 
sq. ft. of retail across 13 or more cities, approximately 9 
million sq. ft. of offices, hotels comprising over 2,000 keys 
and close to 7 million sq. ft. of residential development.
Alongside projects already under execution, we continue 
to selectively evaluate opportunities in markets such as 
Delhi-NCR, Hyderabad, Navi Mumbai and Jaipur. Expansion 
will remain disciplined and focused on locations where 
we believe we can create differentiated destinations and 
attractive long-term returns.Capital Allocation
The programme described above will require substantial 
investment over the next several years. Our first priority 
is to fund this growth through cash generated by our 
operating businesses, supplemented by debt and partner 
capital where appropriate.
Our financial position gives us the capacity to pursue 
this programme. During FY26, operating free cash flow 
increased by 23% to H2,140 crore, while Net Debt to EBITDA 
improved to 1.19x, despite the investments being made 
across our development pipeline.
During FY26, following receipt of the requisite regulatory 
and shareholder approvals, we completed the first tranche 
of the transaction announced last year to facilitate 
CPP Investments' exit from ISMDPL. The payment was 
completed in November 2025, increasing our ownership 
from 51% to 58.33%. The remaining consideration is 
payable through three further tranches and is expected to 
be funded substantially through surplus cash and strong 
internal accruals generated by ISMDPL, together with the 
platform’s capacity to raise additional debt.
ISMDPL today comprises approximately 4.4 million sq. ft. of 
operational retail and 2.2 million sq. ft. of completed offices, 
together with significant further development potential. 
Increasing our ownership allows us to participate more 
fully in the future earnings, cash flows and value creation 
of a platform and assets we know well.
We continue to partner with CPP Investments in Project 
Rise in Mumbai and Phoenix Grand Victoria in Kolkata. 
Partner capital will continue to have a role where it enables 
us to pursue attractive opportunities while maintaining 
appropriate balance-sheet flexibility.
Alongside reinvestment in the business, shareholder 
distributions remain an important component of our 
capital-allocation framework. For FY26, the Board 
has recommended a dividend of H2.50 per share. Our 
objective is to balance reinvestment, growth, leverage and 
shareholder distributions while preserving the financial 
flexibility required to execute the opportunities ahead.
People and Leadership
As Phoenix has grown, so has the scale and complexity of 
the platform we operate. Sustaining this growth requires 
strong leadership teams, clear accountability and a culture 
that combines entrepreneurial thinking with disciplined 
execution.
I continue to mentor and guide the CEOs and leadership 
teams of our retail, office, hospitality, residential and projects 
businesses, working closely with them on the priorities that 
shape each business. Several leaders have spent more 
than a decade at Phoenix and taken on progressively larger 
responsibilities as the Company has grown.We are equally focused on developing the next generation 
of leaders across our businesses and functions and 
creating opportunities for them to assume greater 
responsibility as we expand.
I am particularly pleased that during the year, Shishir 
Shrivastava was elevated to Vice Chairman. Shishir has 
been an integral part of Phoenix for more than twenty-
seven years and has made an invaluable contribution 
to building the Company and its businesses. As Non-
Executive Vice Chairman, his deep operating experience, 
institutional knowledge and long-term perspective continue 
to strengthen our Board and contribute meaningfully to our 
strategic thinking.
Our objective is to build an institution that can continue 
creating value over decades, supported by strong 
leadership, a culture of ownership and the ability to develop 
talent from within.
Our Responsibility to Society and the 
Environment
Through our partnership with the Aakar Charitable 
Trust, our contributions during the year supported 
the construction of more than 250 check dams and 
ponds across Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Gujarat, 
strengthening water security and agricultural 
resilience and benefiting more than 88,000 people. We 
also continue to support initiatives in education, rural 
development and social welfare.
PHOENIX GRAND VICTORIA, KOLKATA
Across our portfolio, we are increasing green-building 
certification and the use of renewable energy while 
improving the resource efficiency of our operating assets 
and new developments.
In Closing
We enter FY27 with a strong operating portfolio, recently 
completed office assets continuing to ramp up and a 
substantial development programme under execution.
Our priorities are clear: continue improving the 
performance of the assets we already own, deliver our 
projects with discipline on cost and timelines, lease new 
developments well ahead of completion and maintain a 
strong balance sheet as we grow.
If we execute these priorities consistently, the value created 
by the platform will continue to compound over time.
I thank our teams across India for their commitment 
and execution, our tenants, customers, business and 
financial partners for their continued confidence and our 
shareholders for their support.
With gratitude,
ATUL RUIA
Chairman

SHISHIR SHRIVASTAVA
Vice Chairman
Dear Shareholders,
It is a privilege to write to you for the first time as Vice 
Chairman. Having worked across Phoenix’s businesses for 
over twenty-seven years, I continue to be closely engaged 
with the Company’s strategy and development. In this 
letter, I want to focus on the operating progress behind 
FY26 and the drivers that should shape the next phase of 
earnings and cash-flow growth.
FY26 demonstrated the breadth of the platform. Retail 
delivered record consumption, offices moved from 
development into leasing and income ramp-up, hospitality 
strengthened further and residential generated strong cash flows. The common thread was not simply greater 
scale, but better productivity from existing assets and 
disciplined execution across the portfolio.
Retail: Understanding the Growth Drivers
Retail consumption reached H16,587 crore in FY26, up 21% 
year-on-year, while retail rental income grew 10% to H2,157 
crore and asset-level retail EBITDA grew 12% to H2,246 
crore. This was achieved without adding new mall capacity 
during the year. We also concluded approximately 920 
leasing deals covering 3.2 million sq. ft. and opened more 
than 400 stores.Growth was broad-based. Phoenix Mall of Asia led the 
portfolio, with consumption increasing 95% to H2,213 crore 
as trading occupancy improved by 10 percentage points. 
Phoenix Mall of the Millennium grew consumption by 30%, 
while Phoenix Palladium, our most established destination, 
grew by 16%. This combination is important: our newer 
assets continue to ramp up, while mature assets are still 
finding ways to grow.
The category mix was equally encouraging. Fashion & 
Accessories, which accounts for nearly 60% of trading 
area, grew 16%; cinema and entertainment grew 22%, while 
jewellery and electronics grew by more than 30%. Even 
excluding jewellery and electronics, consumption grew 
15%, indicating that the year’s growth was not dependent 
on a narrow set of categories.
At Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and Phoenix Avenue 
of Stars, Pune, we deliberately accepted lower trading 
occupancy while rechurning space and upgrading the 
brand mix. The objective was to improve rental productivity 
rather than protect occupancy for its own sake. The early 
evidence is encouraging. In Q1 FY27, rental income and 
trading density at Phoenix Avenue of Stars grew by 13% 
and 26%, respectively; at Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore 
they grew by 17% and 15%, respectively. Across the portfolio, trading density reached approximately H3,750 
pspm at Phoenix Palladium and crossed H3,000 pspm at 
both Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and Phoenix Mall of 
Asia in Q1 FY27.
There is also a structural runway from the assets we 
already own. Around 50% of our current retail GLA comes 
up for renewal over FY27 to FY29. Renewals create an 
opportunity to reset base rents, refresh the brand and 
category mix and capture higher re-leasing spreads without 
new development capital. Store openings, occupancy 
recovery, asset repositioning and lease renewals therefore 
provide multiple, visible drivers of rental growth.
Offices: Built, Leased and Now Ramping
Our completed office portfolio expanded from 
approximately 2 million sq. ft. in March 2024 to 
approximately 4.8 million sq. ft., following the completion of 
Phoenix Asia Towers, Millennium Towers and One National 
Park during 2025. We completed approximately 2.2 million 
sq. ft. of gross leasing during FY26 and ended the year with 
portfolio occupancy of approximately 70%.
The established office assets in Mumbai and Pune reached 
83% leased occupancy, while the three assets completed

during 2025 reached 62%. Our established office portfolio 
generated H213 crore of income and H141 crore of EBITDA 
in FY26. Importantly, signed leases do not translate into 
income immediately: tenants first complete fit-outs and 
move into the space. As this happens, a significant part of 
the leasing achieved in FY26 should progressively convert 
into earnings. We saw the beginning of this in Q1 FY27, when 
office income grew 44% year-on-year.
We are also building a differentiated workplace 
proposition. The integration of our offices with Phoenix’s 
retail-led campuses, complemented by amenities such 
as The Great Hall and the Millennium Club, is designed to 
improve the occupier experience and support retention. As 
the portfolio stabilises, offices should become a materially 
larger annuity contributor to Phoenix.
Hospitality: Strengthening the Destination
Hospitality income grew 8% to H596 crore, with EBITDA 
increasing 14% to H276 crore. The St. Regis, Mumbai led 
the portfolio, with income of H540 crore and EBITDA of 
H262 crore. Its EBITDA margin improved to 49% from 45% 
in FY25, demonstrating the operating leverage available in 
a mature, high-quality hotel asset.A luxury hotel also changes the operating rhythm of an 
entire mixed-use campus: banqueting and events bring 
weekend demand, corporate travel anchors weekdays, and 
restaurants extend activity beyond mall trading hours. That 
is why hospitality matters to us beyond room economics 
alone, and why the Grand Hyatt Bangalore will be an 
important part of our expanding Whitefield campus.
Residential: Selective and Cash Generative
Our residential business delivered gross bookings of 
H471 crore in FY26, with collections of H467 crore and 
an average sales price of approximately H28,600 per 
sq. ft. Importantly, residential contributed H282 crore to 
operating free cash flow during the year, more than three 
times the contribution in FY25.
Residential plays a complementary role in our portfolio. In 
the right locations, it allows us to monetise embedded value 
and generate cash that can be recycled into our annuity 
businesses, without making residential scale an objective in 
itself. We will therefore remain selective, while the next phases 
in Bengaluru and Kolkata provide continuity to the business.Capital Allocation: Funding Growth with Discipline
FY26 was also a year of significant capital deployment. 
Following receipt of the requisite approvals, we completed 
the first tranche payment of the ISMDPL transaction in 
November 2025, deploying H1,257 crore and increasing our 
ownership from 51% to 58.33%. We also deployed H1,035 
crore towards construction expenditure and H431 crore 
towards land, FSI and development rights.
The more important point is that this investment was 
undertaken while maintaining balance-sheet discipline. 
Operating free cash flow increased 23% to H2,140 crore, 
Net Debt to EBITDA improved to 1.19x from 1.24x, and our 
cost of debt declined to 7.51%. At March 2026, gross debt 
stood at H5,164 crore and net debt at H3,160 crore.
The remaining consideration for the ISMDPL acquisition 
is payable through three further tranches. ISMDPL is 
generating strong internal accruals and also has the 
capacity to raise additional debt. We therefore expect 
a substantial part of the remaining consideration to be 
funded by the platform itself. More broadly, internal cash 
generation remains our principal source of funding, 
supplemented by debt and partner capital where 
appropriate. The objective is to match capital deployment 
with the cash-generation profile and progress of the 
underlying assets.
Execution Across the Development Pipeline
For me, the key measure of the development pipeline is not 
only its size, but how progressively it is being de-risked. We 
are witnessing strong retailer interest, and healthy pre-
leasing momentum across our upcoming developments. 
Phoenix Grand Victoria, Kolkata is approaching 90% 
pre-leasing and Surat is approaching 50%, well ahead of 
completion. Thane has secured environmental clearance 
and is moving towards excavation; construction activity 
is already progressing at Coimbatore and Chandigarh. At 
Lower Parel and Whitefield, expansion projects are also 
moving through construction and pre-leasing.
Each of these milestones removes a different layer of risk: 
approvals establish the right to build, construction creates 
delivery visibility and pre-leasing establishes the path to 
income. Our objective is not simply to complete buildings, 
but to open them with strong tenant commitments and a 
clear path to stabilised cash flows.
The People Behind the Performance
The performance across our businesses reflects the 
depth of experience within the teams that run them. I 
have worked alongside many of these colleagues for 
several years and have seen their responsibilities grow 
with the businesses themselves. That continuity creates 
institutional knowledge that is difficult to replicate and 
becomes more valuable as the platform grows in scale and 
complexity.
That experience extends well beyond the senior leadership 
team. Across our cities, teams lease space, deliver 
projects, operate destinations and serve customers 
every day. Our performance this year was the result of 
that collective execution. Working with these teams and 
supporting the next generation of leadership remains one 
of the most rewarding parts of my role as Vice Chairman.
Building Responsibly at Scale
Sustainability is integral to how we build and operate. 
Around 39% of our portfolio GLA is USGBC LEED® certified, 
with certifications achieved at Phoenix Asia Towers, 
Millennium Towers and One National Park.
Our transition towards cleaner energy also continues. 
Renewable energy met around 37% of the covered 
electricity load at assets where green power 
arrangements were operational. During the year, we 
started receiving green energy supply at The St. Regis, 
Mumbai and at Phoenix Mall of the Millennium and 
Millennium Towers in Pune. We remain focused on 
extending adoption across the portfolio.
In Closing
The next phase of growth is already visible across the 
platform. We have several operating assets with further 
productivity to unlock, recently completed offices moving 
into income generation and a development pipeline that is 
progressively being de-risked.
We will continue to hold to the discipline that brought us 
here: invest where we see attractive long-term returns, 
fund growth prudently, protect the balance sheet and 
maintain high standards of execution across every 
destination.
My thanks go to our teams, whose execution turns plans 
into places, and to our shareholders, partners, tenants and 
customers for their continued confidence in Phoenix.
Yours truly,
SHISHIR SHRIVASTAVA
Vice Chairman

OUR APPROACH TO 
MATERIAL TOPICS
A materiality assessment sharpens a wide field of sustainability 
priorities into the handful that matter the most to our business and our 
stakeholders. It shapes how we allocate resources, set goals and report 
progress, ensuring ESG considerations are integrated into business 
processes rather than treated as standalone initiatives.
Our material topics have been identified through a 
structured assessment that draws on investor and tenant 
engagement, peer benchmarking and leadership input 
across functions and evaluated through a dual lens: 
stakeholder relevance and business impact. Each material topic has been reviewed based on its 
potential impact on long-term value creation, enabling us 
to prioritise matters that guide strategic decision-making 
and shape our reporting disclosures.

Our balance sheet remained disciplined through a

H2,723 crore across: (i) the first tranche of the ISMDPL

expenditure (H1,035 crore), and (iii) acquisition of land and

Approximately 93% of borrowings remain linked to annuity 
generating operational assets, providing strong visibility of 
cash flows available to service debt . The average cost of 
debt declined from 8.50% to 7.51% during FY26, continuing 
its reduction from 9.20% in FY20. This improvement was 
supported by proactive refinancing, reduction in repo rate 
and a calibrated lease rental discounting (LRD) strategy. As 
of 31 March 2026, gross debt stood at H5,164 crore, while 
liquidity stood at H2,004 crore.
This financial prudence was further reflected in rating 
actions, with nine Group entities receiving one-notch 
upgrades across CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings and CARE. 
Further, 16 of the 18 rated Group entities now carry ratings 
of A or above, while ratings across Group subsidiaries 
range from BBB+ to AA-. Thoth Mall and Commercial Real

Cost Discipline and Efficiency
Cost discipline is embedded in our operating model. Our 
annuity-led business model, where majority of the revenue 
is recurring and contractual, generates natural operating 
leverage. A meaningful portion of property-level operating 
costs is fixed or semi-fixed, enabling incremental revenue 
from higher consumption and occupancy to convert efficiently 
into EBITDA. Tenant-mix optimisation across the Phoenix 
MarketCity portfolio, and centralised systems for accounting, 
property management, procurement and cash-flow 
management support this discipline as the portfolio scales.

STRATEGIC INVESTMENTS 
Our development pipeline provides a clear pathway for 
growth through 2030 and beyond across three dimensions: 
new retail destinations, the densification of existing assets 
and the expansion of our commercial office, hospitality and 
residential portfolios.
Capital is deployed in phases. Land acquisitions are 
primarily funded through internal accruals. Construction 
begins after design and regulatory approvals, and tendering 
provides visibility on 50–60% of project costs. Debt is drawn 
progressively as execution advances towards completion. 
This sequencing aligns funding with project milestones and 
limits idle capital, supporting efficient capital deployment 
through the development cycle.ESG PRINCIPLE 
Sustainability is integrated into capital allocation, asset 
design and operating-cost management. Approximately 
39% of our operational retail and commercial office 
portfolio, measured by GLA, is currently USGBC LEED® 
certified, against an aspiration of reaching 50% over 
the long term. Renewable energy met around 37% of the 
covered electricity load at assets where green-power 
arrangements were operational.

We enter FY27 with an operating portfolio that generates 
strong cash flows, a resilient balance sheet and a clearly 
sequenced development pipeline. Near-term earnings 
growth will be driven largely from assets already in the 
ground: repositioned spaces across the Phoenix MarketCity 
portfolio contributing for a full year, upcoming lease 
renewals offering a multi-year pathway for rental uplift 
without incremental development capital, and further 
stabilisation at Phoenix Mall of Asia, where the addition of 
luxury and global flagship brands is expected to improve 
trading density and lift trading occupancy to 94–95%. The 
recently expanded office portfolio is entering its revenue 
ramp-up phase, with leasing and occupancy gains expected 
to drive rental-income growth. The operating hotels are 
likewise positioned to benefit from continued focus on guest 
experience, revenue enhancement and operating efficiency.
PHOENIX PALLADIUM, MUMBAIBeyond this base, new capacity extends the runway. New 
retail destinations at Kolkata and Surat, together with the 
retail expansions of Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and 
Phoenix Palladium, will build the near-term earnings base, 
with Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore extending this 
further. Project Rise at Lower Parel and the next phase of 
offices at the expanded Bengaluru campus will strengthen 
the annuity portfolio, and Grand Hyatt Bangalore will broaden 
the hospitality platform. In residential, the focus remains on 
monetising the remaining premium inventory in Bengaluru, 
with selective launches planned in Bengaluru and Kolkata. 
Together, these levers provide visibility beyond the existing 
operating portfolio and position the Company to sustain 
earnings growth through 2030 while maintaining financial 
discipline.Refer to the Natural Capital Chapter in this Integrated Report for

HUMAN CAPITAL 
People capability is a competitive advantage in our business. Our 
retail, office, hospitality and residential assets are experienced 
by consumers, retailers and tenants through the teams that 
operate them, and the quality of that experience shows up in 
footfall conversion, tenant retention and asset performance. 
FY26 was a year of deepening functional capability, widening 
the reach of our wellbeing and engagement platforms, and 
putting digital infrastructure in place across recruitment and 
learning. As PML significantly expands its portfolio, our ability to 
attract, develop and retain talent becomes a critical enabler of 
operational excellence and long-term value creation.UN SDGs Strategic Pillars

WORKFORCE MANAGEMENT 
Workforce management is aligned with the operating 
requirements of our businesses. Our corporate and 
asset teams support our assets across operations, 
leasing, asset management, projects, finance, business 
development and corporate activities.
Our full-time teams hold the critical, customer-facing 
and asset-control roles, protecting continuity, service 
consistency and asset oversight. Contract manpower is 
deployed for select activities, governed by defined service 
standards and compliance frameworks. 
Each asset plans its own manpower through annual 
operating plans, reviewed against business requirements, 
seasonal demand and new asset additions. For assets 
under development, workforce requirements and budgets 
are finalised upfront to ensure timely deployment. Plans 
remain flexible and are recalibrated through the year in 
response to demand and prevailing market conditions. WORKFORCE STABILITY AND LEADERSHIP 
CONTINUITY
Our annuity assets operate on long gestation cycles. 
Assets conceived in one business environment may be 
delivered and stabilised in another, and much of the 
institutional knowledge that carries a project across 
that span sits with individuals. Several members of our 
senior leadership have been with PML for a decade or 
longer, working across multiple phases of portfolio growth 
from acquisition through commissioning to stabilisation. 
This depth of experience supports consistent execution 
and sound judgement across cycles, while reducing 
the risk associated with key transitions. During FY26, 
88 colleagues received Long Service Awards for being 
associated with PML for 5, 10, 15 and 25 years.
Internal mobility has further supported talent development, 
with the Internal Job Posting (IJP) programme enabling 
employees to explore opportunities across businesses and 
functions. During the year, 29 positions were filled through 
IJP, reinforcing our focus on developing and retaining talent 
from within.
Continuity is also reflected in the return of former colleagues. 
Over the last decade, 244 employees have rejoined Phoenix, 
many for their second or third innings. Their return speaks to 
the strength of our culture, the lasting connect people build 
here, and the trust, stability and growth opportunities we offer 
as an employer.
Performance and Accountability 
Performance management is embedded in our day-to-day operations rather than limited to an annual exercise. Each role has 
clearly defined responsibilities and measurable KPIs, supported by continuous feedback and periodic formal assessments. 
This approach helps guide compensation reviews, career progression and development opportunities. FY26 Age Profile — Balanced Experience with

728Total Employees2,073CAPABILITY BUILDING
Capability development is aligned with the requirements of the business across functions and locations. Training 
sessions are designed to strengthen functional capabilities, operational execution and leadership readiness. 
GyaanSetu — Our Digital Learning Platform
GyaanSetu marks an important step in building a digital 
learning environment for all employees, ensuring that 
the right knowledge is available on a single, accessible 
platform. The platform brings together learning modules, 
leadership content, videos, infographics and curated 
external resources, including TEDx and Harvard Business 
Review material, enabling employees across locations to 
learn at their own pace. By offering multiple mediums of 
learning such as e-learning modules, virtual instructor-led 
sessions, classroom programmes, hybrid formats, short 
videos, bite-sized learning, functional and behavioural 
training, and quick masterclasses, GyaanSetu supports 
on-the-go learning and provides employees with timely 
guidance to strengthen their skills and capabilities.Mandatory Modules

SPARK builds role-specific and technical skills through structured learning journeys, designed and delivered in-house 
by our subject-matter experts and regional business leaders. With people who operate our assets directly leading the 
sessions, the content is grounded in practical operating context that external providers may not offer. More than 75 
sessions were delivered during the year addressing operational effectiveness, customer experience and functional depth.

Safety and EHS Capability
Safety training is non-negotiable and is treated as an 
essential operating capability, supported by mandatory 
training, repeated practice and verification. Programmes 
are conducted for employees, contractors and facility 
teams, supported by regular drills, simulations and 
awareness campaigns. 
Our teams conduct hazard identification and risk 
assessments regularly across locations, with defined 
preventive and corrective action frameworks. Safety 
requirements are embedded in contractor agreements 
through pre-induction training, continuous monitoring 
mechanisms and compliance enforcement protocols. 
Emergency response procedures, evacuation protocols 
and incident management systems, including root-cause 
analysis, are implemented across sites to maintain high 
workplace safety standards and reinforce preparedness.

Phoenix Cares
Phoenix Cares has evolved from a daily steps challenge into a holistic wellness suite, reflecting our view that employee 
wellbeing extends beyond physical health. Financial pressure, isolation and stress can affect people at work just as directly, 
making access to timely support an important part of a healthy workplace.
Doctor on Site provides employees with immediate access to medical care across all locations, helping address minor 
ailments early and supporting workplace wellbeing. Introduced initially at our Mumbai locations, the programme has now 
been extended across the organisation. Alongside it, the VISIT app brings consultations, diagnostic tests and pharmacy 
services onto a single platform at subsidised rates, and on-site provision continues through health check-up camps and 
blood donation drives.

STRUCTURED TALENT ACQUISITION 
In a competitive talent environment, employer positioning 
matters as much as the recruitment process. During the

Talent is sourced through recruitment platforms, 
professional networks, employee referrals and our 
internal database. Roles are also posted internally before 
external hiring, making internal mobility the first option 
considered wherever appropriate. Project Phoenix Hire
The implementation of Oracle Recruiting Cloud 
consolidated a recruitment lifecycle that previously ran 
on manual workflows and multiple systems. This covers 
requisition creation, sourcing, interview management, 
offer processing and pre-onboarding. Stage-wise tracking 
provides visibility into hiring progress, timelines and 
conversion ratios, enabling timely intervention when a 
pipeline slows. Integrations with recruitment platforms, 
virtual interview tools and background-verification 
systems allow candidates to move from sourcing through 
verification within one connected workflow. Automated 
document processes also ensure joining formalities are 
completed well in advance.
Together these changes reduced our time-to-offer from six 
to seven days to two days. In a competitive talent market, 
this speed can make a meaningful difference in securing the 
right candidates. Phoenix Her Space
Introduced during FY26, Phoenix Her Space supports

flexible working, wellness support and dedicated HR 
assistance during and after maternity. The programme is

their progression through that transition. Phase 2 will 
extend the same principle to other life stages.

Our organisation is shaped by the spaces we build and the 
relationships that sustain them. They give our destinations 
a sense of place, our partnerships resilience and our 
communities a meaningful stake in our progress. We regard 
these relationships as a form of capital, built patiently and 
strengthened over time.
How the model works 
ACT’s approach is rooted in community ownership and 
behavioural transformation.
Engagement First: Volunteers of ACT engage with villagers 
to build trust and raise awareness about the benefits of 
water harvesting before any construction begins. This also 
includes establishing the necessary preconditions for social 
reform (discouraging practices such as child marriage, 
dowry, substance abuse and funeral feast). Over time, ACT’s 
proven experience in constructing check dams have led 
communities to approach them directly for support.
Joint Contribution: ACT funds 70% of the costs, while the 
remaining 30% is contributed by the villages. This shared 
contribution fosters ownership and accountability.
Rigorous Planning: Every site is assessed on feasibility, 
economic, social and environmental factors before 
implementation. 
Quality Construction: Structures are designed by experts  
with experience, using the best quality materials, ensuring 
transparency, durability and  
cost-effectiveness.
Lasting Outcome: During the monsoons, completed check 
dams retain water and help recharge groundwater and 
village wells. The improved availability of water transforms 
previously dry and arid land into irrigated farmland, 
increasing the area under irrigation from 2% to as much as 
98% in some project locations. This has enabled farmers 
to move beyond a single cropping season, achieve multiple 
harvests, and increase their incomes.OUR RELATIONSHIP ECOSYSTEM
Our approach to value creation rests on four interconnected 
pillars. Together, they shape how we operate, engage with 
our stakeholders and grow as an organisation.
COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS
Our approach to social responsibility is built on long-
term partnerships with organisations that bring local 
knowledge, trust and specialised expertise. The following 
are select initiatives through which we support our 
communities and illustrate our broader approach to 
creating meaningful and lasting impact.
Water Security
Our long-standing commitment to water security is delivered 
through Aakar Charitable Trust (ACT), founded by Ms. Amla 
Ruia. ACT works across 11 states, constructing check dams 
and, where local conditions do not permit them, developing 
ponds as an alternative.
In India’s drought-prone districts, water scarcity is an 
economic challenge as much as an environmental one. 
Without reliable access to water, farming households 
may be limited to a single cropping season, keeping 
incomes low and increasing the risk of migration. 
Securing water at source can strengthen livelihoods 
and improve food security. This remains our largest 
thematic focus. Impact Created – Attributable to PML and Group Entity Funding 
Across ACT as a whole, 810 check dams and 605 ponds were complete as at 31 March 2026, impacting around 1,363 villages 
and transforming lives of around 19.29 lakh people. The work is concentrated in Rajasthan, with 940 sites across 968 villages, 
followed by Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Villages Impacted

COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AT OUR 
DESTINATIONS
Our destinations are part of the communities in which they 
operate. Beyond commerce, they provide spaces for safety 
awareness, participation, learning and shared experiences. 
Drawing on the expertise gained from managing large, 
high-footfall environments, our asset teams work closely 
with local neighbourhoods through safety awareness, civic 
participation and inclusive outreach programmes. In addition 
to our CSR initiatives, our asset teams undertake a range of 
community-focused activities independent of the Group CSR 
budget. The examples below are illustrative of this work.
Sharing Safety Capability with our Neighbours
We manage complex, high-footfall destinations on a daily 
basis. Fire and life safety is a core area of operational 
expertise across our destinations. During the year, 
we conducted structured fire and safety awareness 
programmes for schools and residential communities, 
helping improve emergency preparedness across the 
wider neighbourhood. Creating Shared Community Spaces
Our spaces serve as places where people come together 
to connect, participate and celebrate shared experiences. 
Through thoughtfully curated events, cultural programmes 
and community-led activities, we encourage greater public 
participation while reinforcing the social relevance of our 
destinations within the cities they are built in. 
At Phoenix MarketCity Mumbai, we hosted community 
chess through the year. This included a weekly club and 
tournaments organised with ChessBase India, open to 
participants of all ages and skill levels. The initiative was 
conducted every Saturday during FY26, with average 
participation of around 300 children and their families. 
Started in 2022, it has since built a community of more than 
2,500 members across age groups. 
Collaborating with Civic Institutions
We work closely with civic authorities and public safety 
agencies. At Phoenix United, Bareilly, we instituted the 
Special 26 Awards to recognise police and allied public 
safety departments, including traffic police, fire services and 
disaster management personnel. The initiative recognises 
their contribution while fostering closer coordination with 
the agencies responsible for public safety. 
This collaboration extends across the portfolio through 
initiatives such as traffic management and joint operations 
with municipal and police authorities at Phoenix Palladium, 
Mumbai, as well as the beautification of a 3.2 km stretch 
of the Eastern Express Highway at Phoenix MarketCity, 
Mumbai. 
Promoting Inclusion
We work to keep our destinations welcoming for everyone. 
At Phoenix United Bareilly, our Phoenix Smile initiative 
hosted a Children’s Day celebration. Children from the 
local community enjoyed entertainment zones, a magician 
show, gifts and play sessions. These inclusive experiences 
strengthen neighbourhood ties. Impact
At Palladium Ahmedabad, the safety team conducted

OUR INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL ECOSYSTEM
Market Intelligence & Disciplined Growth
Operating a portfolio of retail, offices, hotels and 
residential, across nine cities in India gives us a first-
hand insight into changing consumer preferences, retail 
categories and urban catchments. We apply these insights 
to decisions relating to tenant mix, zoning, customer 
engagement and experience creation.
As discretionary spending  shifts towards premium and 
experience-led categories, we have expanded dining, 
entertainment, leisure and social formats within our 
destinations. We also refresh category and brand mix 
as catchments evolve, including where rising affluence 
creates opportunities for premiumisation.
Where demand supports it, we densify our retail assets 
with complementary uses such as offices and hotels, 
strengthening the destination as a whole.
Our market understanding also informs new-city entry. 
Through our framework, we assess a market’s economic 
anchors, catchment strength, infrastructure readiness, 
competitive intensity, regulatory environment and retailer 
appetite.
Our established relationships with retailers provide 
an additional perspective on market demand, category 
trends and brand-expansion priorities. These insights 
help us evaluate the depth of demand within a market and 
determine  how a potential destination may fit within the 
broader portfolio.
We combine market understanding with disciplined capital 
allocation. Each opportunity is assessed against expected 
returns, funding availability, execution feasibility and REPOSITIONING: RENEWING VALUE WITHIN THE 
PORTFOLIO
Our repositioning approach begins with asset-level insight. We 
assess category performance, tenant productivity, customer 
preferences and the evolution of each catchment to determine 
where space can be put to better use. These insights guide 
the deliberate replacement of lower-productivity formats with 
higher-yielding inline stores, flagship formats, new experiences, 
and brands aligned with the positioning of the destination.
During the year, we completed a substantial part of the 
planned repositioning at Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and 
Phoenix Avenue of Stars, Pune, with approximately 30% of 
the area at each asset undergoing churn. The programme 
included the introduction of flagship formats and marquee 
brands, together with a more productive allocation of space.
The execution involved a deliberate near-term trade-off in 
trading occupancy as spaces were recast and new stores 
introduced. Despite this transition, rentals and EBITDA 
remained stable, and trading density improved by 23% at 
Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and 17% at Phoenix Avenue of 
Stars in FY26.
In May 2026, Phoenix MarketCity Pune was rebranded 
and relaunched as Phoenix Avenue of Stars, Pune, with an 
portfolio fit. New markets may be entered through a retail-
led first phase, with the flexibility to introduce offices, hotels 
or other uses as the local ecosystem matures.
This phased approach helps us manage execution risk, deploy 
resources efficiently and respond to market absorption. 
It supports our ambition to double our annuity portfolio, 
comprising retail and office assets, by 2030, while diversifying 
cash flows across hospitality and residential development.
PHOENIX PRIDE OF INDIA, INDOREDESIGN, CURATION AND EXPERIENCE IPS
A repeatable capability that keeps our destinations 
relevant
Retail destinations must evolve as customers, brands 
and catchments change. We have built a repeatable 
capability to create, activate and refresh our destinations, 
strengthening their relevance over time. This approach 
rests on design, tenant curation, destination marketing 
and year-round programming. Design and curation shape 
the physical and merchandising environment. Marketing 
and programming activate it. Together, they give 
customers compelling reasons to return time and again. 
Design and curation: shaping productive environments
Design and tenant curation influence how effectively 
each floorplate performs. Our in-house zoning expertise 
transforms standard floorplates into differentiated 
retail environments. We plan spaces around customer 
movement, brand visibility and category adjacencies. 
Watch and jewellery zones, premium beauty and wellness 
clusters and destination-dining areas make categories 
easier to discover while giving participating brands 
greater visibility.
Tenant curation shapes the merchandising mix. We refresh 
the mix as customer preferences evolve. We also introduce 
flagship formats and marquee brands to strengthen each 
destination’s proposition. 
Every mall shares this focus on quality, but each carries 
its own identity. Signature art installations reinforce that 
identity, from Salvador Dalí’s Cosmic Rhinoceros at Phoenix 
Palladium, Mumbai, to Saddled with Time at Palladium 
Ahmedabad.
Destination marketing 
A well-curated destination comes to life through a 
360-degree marketing and activation programme. It 
combines experiences at the mall with sustained visibility 
across print, outdoor, digital, social media and content-
led campaigns. Hyperlocal influencers extend this reach, 
while celebrities support select high-impact moments. 
We also collaborate with retail partners on campaigns, 
launches and promotions. Cinema, entertainment, dining 
and experiential formats broaden the destination’s appeal 
beyond shopping. Together, these efforts attract footfall 
across different days and times.
Experience IPs and year-round programming
Our owned Experience IPs form a structured, year-round 
engagement calendar. They span categories, seasons, 
occasions and customer groups. Category-led IPs such 
as The Beauty Edit, The Great Electronics Fest and The 
Phoenix Food Fest activate priority retail segments. 
Flagship seasonal campaigns such as Holiday Land and 
the Phoenix Shopping Festival create a consistent rhythm 
of engagement across the year. Festive and topical IPs, 
including Navratri Festival, Women’s Day, Independence upgraded façade, refreshed interiors and enhanced brand mix, 
reflecting its evolution into a more premium, experience-led 
destination.
With leases covering approximately 50% of our current 
operational retail GLA due for renewal over the next three 
years, this capability gives us a multi-year opportunity to 
refresh tenant mix and capture rental uplift without significant 
incremental development capital.

DIGITAL CAPABILITIES AND DATA GOVERNANCE
Technology supports the efficiency, reliability and 
resilience of our platform. Our investments are focused on 
strengthening connectivity, reporting, collaboration, data 
protection and decision-making.
The deployment of gigabit passive optical network 
infrastructure has reduced network costs by 
approximately 25% to 30% while improving uptime. 
Collaboration tools have helped reduce travel costs, while 
our migration to SAP S/4HANA has substantially improved 
reporting speed.
Our cybersecurity and data-protection practices are 
aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and 
CIS Controls. These include continuous monitoring 
through a 24×7 Security Operations Centre, annual 
penetration testing, IT general-controls audits and cloud 
backup arrangements that enable data recovery within 
approximately four hours.
Our roadmap includes the responsible use of Agentic AI for 
suitable routine activities and decision support, as well as 
smart-mall capabilities focused on energy optimisation and 
reducing downtime. Data governance, information security 
and appropriate human oversight will remain central to

Dining as a Destination
GOURMET VILLAGE: FROM CONSUMER INSIGHT 
TO A SCALABLE FORMAT
Gourmet Village at Phoenix Palladium demonstrated how 
we converted an emerging shift in consumer behaviour 
into a differentiated format and used the resulting learning 
to inform other destinations across the portfolio.
Our operating experience indicated that consumers were 
increasingly visiting malls not only to shop, but also to dine, 
socialise, participate in social activities and spend time 
with family and friends. Food, entertainment and active-
lifestyle experiences were becoming primary drivers of 
visitation rather than supplementary conveniences. This 
prompted a more fundamental question: could dining be 
designed as a destination anchor in its own right? TURNING INSIGHT INTO A DESTINATION
Launched in July 2025, Gourmet Village occupies ~85,000 
sq. ft., spread over two floors, at Phoenix Palladium, 
Mumbai. This space brings together over 19 brands within 
a curated dining environment. It forms part of a wider 
experiential proposition that includes Game Palacio, 
a family entertainment destination, and Phoenix HSBC 
Racquet Club, which introduced 6 pickleball and 6 paddle 
courts to the mall. 
The format was conceived as an integrated destination 
rather than a collection of independent outlets. Restaurant 
curation, zoning, circulation, ambience and neighbouring 
entertainment uses were considered together, allowing 
customers to combine dining with play, sport and social 
engagement during a single visit.
GOURMET VILLAGE, PHOENIX PALLADIUM, MUMBAICOMBINING MULTIPLE CAPABILITIES
Gourmet Village brings together several capabilities 
developed across our platform:
The intellectual capital lies in the integration of these 
capabilities. No individual restaurant, design intervention 
or entertainment use defines the proposition. Its 
distinctiveness is created through the way these elements 
work together.ESTABLISHING COMMERCIAL RELEVANCE
Gourmet Village has developed into a meaningful 
contributor to consumption and rentals at Phoenix 
Palladium, supporting dwell time and repeat visits. Its 
impact is reinforced by the wider experiential ecosystem 
at the destination: dining, family entertainment and 
active-lifestyle uses together expand the occasions the 
destination serves and create opportunities for cross-
engagement between them.
SCALING THE GOURMET VILLAGE CONCEPT
Having validated the format at Phoenix Palladium, we are 
applying the underlying learning across the portfolio, 
beginning with Phoenix Palassio and Phoenix MarketCity 
Bangalore (spread over 0.17 mn sq. ft.), while Phoenix Mall 
of the Millennium and Phoenix Mall of Asia already embed 
dining as a destination concept by design. Each destination 
serves a different catchment, so the objective is not to 
replicate Gourmet Village but to transfer its philosophy: 
treating dining and leisure as integrated anchors, curating 
complementary uses around the customer occasion, 
and designing more extended, varied visits. This is the 
more durable capability: knowing what to transfer, what 
to modify, and how to bring design, leasing, curation and 
operations together for a particular asset.

ENERGY CONSUMPTION
Total electricity consumption across our operational 
retail, commercial office and hospitality portfolio 
stood at 320 GWh in FY26, representing an increase of 
approximately 8% over the previous year. 
The increase was led by continued ramp-up, with higher 
occupancy at Phoenix Mall of the Millennium and Phoenix 
Mall of Asia and the launch of Gourmet Village at Phoenix 
Palladium. This was partly offset by lower consumption at 
two of our retail assets which were under repositioning 
during the year. Our three new commercial offices: 
Phoenix Asia Towers, Millennium Towers and One National 
Park, received their occupancy certifications during 2025 
and were in a ramp-up phase through the year. Their 
electricity consumption is therefore not yet fully reflected, 
and is expected to rise as occupancy stabilises.
As our portfolio grows and diversifies, we remain focused 
on monitoring consumption at asset level and improving 
energy efficiency.

WATER MANAGEMENT 
Our approach focuses on optimising 
consumption through conservation, 
recycling and reuse, enabling us to meet 
the needs of a growing portfolio while 
reducing dependence on freshwater 
resources.
Total water withdrawal across our 
operational retail, commercial office and 
hospitality portfolio stood at 35 lakh KL 
during FY26. The increase was driven by 
higher footfalls and occupancy across our 
retail and office portfolio, growth in food 
and beverage operations, and new offices 
that were operational for part of the year.
We continue to strengthen water 
management practices, improving 
utilisation while supporting the efficient 
operation of our developments.
Smart fixtures — such as sensors, aerators, and waterless 
urinals reducing wastage significantly compared to 
conventional fittings. 
Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) — are operational across 
assets. Wastewater recycled through STPs, is used for cooling 
towers, flushing, landscaping, and gardening and so on.
Rainwater harvesting systems — collected rainwater is 
used for flushing and cooling tower requirements.
Groundwater treatment — Groundwater inflows at select 
locations are treated and repurposed for domestic and 
cooling needs, helping conserve freshwater resources.Our Water Conservation 
Measures

Global real GDP grew by 3.4% in 2025, with advanced 
economies expanding by 1.9%, reflecting the impact of 
elevated interest rates, while emerging markets and 
developing economies grew at a stronger 4.4%, supported 
by domestic demand and infrastructure-led expansion. 
Global economic activity remained resilient amid persistent 
policy and geopolitical uncertainty. Steady demand for 
services, stable labour markets and continued investment 
in technology supported growth.GLOBAL GDP GROWTH

Outlook
Global GDP growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 
and 3.2% in 2027 (IMF), with advanced economies slowing 
to 1.8% and emerging markets and developing economies 
sustaining growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 4.2% in 2027.

amid weaker demand and continued uncertainty.2  Risks 
remain skewed to the downside, driven by geopolitical 
tensions, commodity price volatility, elevated debt levels 
and financial market uncertainty. 
Indian Economy
India sustained strong economic momentum in FY26, with 
real GDP growth estimated at 7.6%, among the fastest 
globally, and ahead of the 3.4% world average.3

consumption-driven sectors.

Consumer and Retail Sentiment
Global Consumer Sentiment
Global consumer sentiment in early 2026 reflects a 
cautious and uneven recovery amid persistent economic 
uncertainty and evolving spending priorities. The Ipsos 
Global Consumer Confidence Index was stable at ~49.4 in 
March 2026, indicating a neutral demand environment.9 
Sentiment continues to diverge across regions. Advanced 
economies remain under pressure from inflation and 
higher borrowing costs, while emerging markets have 
remained relatively resilient, supported by stronger 
domestic demand conditions. India and parts of Southeast 
Asia continue to outperform global averages.
Indian Consumption Landscape
India’s consumption environment remains structurally 
sound, with demand shifting towards organised 
retail, premium formats and experience-led spending. 
Consumption is becoming more differentiated across 
regions, incomes, and categories, requiring more targeted, 
data-driven and localised strategies.
A key transformation is visible in consumer journeys. 
Among digitally active urban consumers, nearly 80% 
discover products via social media and over 70% engage 
across multiple channels before making a purchase. 
Physical retail is adapting in response, with stores being 
increasingly positioned as high-engagement touchpoints 
focused on discovery, experience and conversion rather 
than purely transactional spaces.10

REAL ESTATE IN INDIA16
India’s real estate sector has entered a phase of 
broad-based expansion supported by ₹37,625 crore in 
institutional investment in 2025, improving execution 
quality and creating a more disciplined supply 
environment. In recent years, better alignment between 
demand and supply has led to healthier absorption levels, 
more disciplined development and increased confidence 
among both developers and investors.
India’s real estate market is projected to reach USD 1 
trillion by 2030 and expand further to USD 5–6 trillion by 
2047. From the current contribution of 13% to GDP, the 
sector's share is expected to rise steadily as urbanisation 
deepens and organised development expands.
Urbanisation remains a major structural driver. India’s 
urban population is projected to increase from nearly 543 
million in 2025 to around 900 million by 2047, an addition 
of over 350 million urban residents over two decades. 
This will sustain long-run demand for housing, commercial 
infrastructure and integrated developments, with Tier 
2 and Tier 3 cities emerging as increasingly significant 
contributors alongside established metros.
Investment activity strengthened meaningfully during the

Residential Real Estate in India
India’s residential real estate market in 2025 continued 
to shift towards value-led growth, with pricing, product 
quality and segmental mix gaining more prominence 
over volume. While volumes moderated from peak levels, 
demand remained resilient, supported by rising incomes, 
premiumisation and improving bu yer confidence.
During the year, aggregate sales across the top seven 
cities declined by 14% YoY to around 3.95 lakh units, while 
the total transaction value increased 6%, crossing ₹6 lakh 
crore, a divergence that signals a move towards higher 
ticket sizes and stronger pricing realisation.18 
Premiumisation was a key theme of the year, supported 
by lifestyle aspirations and higher disposable incomes. 
Luxury apartment sales grew approximately 70% YoY, 
with high-end segments accounting for nearly 27% of total 
sales.19 Buyers are prioritising larger homes, superior 
amenities and integrated lifestyle environments over 
entry -level product.

Technology firms led absorption with a 23% share, followed 
by flexible workspace operators at 20% and BFSI at 15%; 
together accounting for nearly 60% of leasing activity. 
Demand from E&M firms, research, consultancy and  
accounting companies, and  life sciences occupiers  
remained steady, reinforcing the depth of non-technology 
office demand across major markets.
A key structural driver of demand remains the continued 
expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs). GCCs leased 
around 32.8 million sq. ft. in 2025, i.e. nearly 39% of the 
total absorption, with Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR 
accounting for around 69% of total GCC leasing in 2025. 
On the supply side, new office completions reached a 
historic high of 58.9 million sq. ft., up 10% YoY. These new development infusions were increasingly dominated by 
high-quality, experience-led assets, featuring superior 
design standards, more efficient floor plates, and 
enhanced  amenity offerings aligned with occupiers’ ‘flight-
to quality’ preferences. Green-certified assets accounted 
for 87% of all new completions.
Leasing activity by domestic companies during the year 
was increasingly driven by business scale-ups, portfolio 
consolidation, and the rising adoption of flexible and 
managed workspace models. This sustained expansion by 
Indian companies helped mitigate global demand  volatility 
and reinforced the structural resilience of the country’s 
office market. 
Per CBRE’s occupier survey, 77% of tenants plan portfolio 
expansion over the next two years.23  India’s office market 
has entered a new era of scale, with stock surpassing the 1 
billion sq. ft. milestone. 24
Retail Real Estate in India
India’s retail real estate market in 2025 saw a shift 
towards asset quality and location, with leasing 
increasingly concentrated in high-performing malls and 
prime high streets, as well-positioned assets continue to 
outperform the broader market.
On the supply side, 4.3 million sq. ft. of new retail space 
was delivered in 2025, concentrated in a few key cities. 
Hyderabad accounted for over half of total supply addition 
in 2025, followed by Mumbai and Delhi-NCR.25 
Geographically, leasing was concentrated in leading 
consumption centres: Hyderabad accounted for 29% 
of total absorption, followed by Mumbai and Delhi-NCR 
at 18% each.26 Within assets, leasing was concentrated 
in mid-sized store formats of 1,000–5,000 sq. ft., 
enabling retailers to balance expansion ambition with 
operational efficiency.27 
The most significant structural shift was the continued 
rise of experiential retail, as entertainment, F&B and 
leisure categories deepened their share of leasing activity, 
increasingly replacing traditional anchor formats and 
redefining how malls generate footfall.
City-level demand reflected localised consumption 
patterns: fashion and lifestyle categories led in NCR and 
Mumbai, while entertainment and family-oriented formats 
gained greater share in Hyderabad and Bengaluru.

Hospitality Sector in India28
India’s hospitality sector maintained strong growth 
momentum throughout 2025, underpinned by robust 
domestic demand and a resilient economic landscape.
Overall occupancy levels improved to ~64% in 2025, 
providing a stable base for revenue growth.
Revenue per available room (RevPAR) rose by 11% 
YoY, surpassing the 9% growth recorded in 2024. 
Similarly, average daily rates (ADR) increased by 8.7% 
YoY, an acceleration from the 6.8% growth seen in the 
previous year.29
By the end of 2025, total branded inventory reached 
~450,000 keys, bolstered by the addition of over 14,400 
new rooms during the year.30 The Upper Midscale, Upper 
Upscale and Upscale categories cumulatively accounted 
for ~60% of new openings, directly addressing the 
heightened consumer appetite for luxury experiences. Tier 
2 cities and emerging leisure destinations are absorbing 
a growing share of new development, supported by 
improving connectivity and diversifying demand patterns. 
Policy tailwinds strengthen the medium-term case. The 
Union Budget 2026–27 prioritises tourism infrastructure, 
destination development and connectivity; measures 
aligned with a broader objective of positioning 
tourism as a meaningful driver of employment and 
regional development. 
Total hotel deal value reached ~USD 456 million 
in 2025, representing a 2.5x YoY growth from 
US$184 million in 2024.
The Indian hospitality sector is positioned for steady 
growth, transitioning from post-pandemic recovery 
towards structural maturity characterised by disciplined 
expansion and pricing stability.PROMINENT SECTORS DRIVING OFFICE ABSORPTION

OPPORTUNITIES AND THREATS 
Rising Consumption and Premiumisation
Growing disposable incomes, urbanisation and increasing discretionary spending across 
fashion, dining, entertainment and lifestyle categories are supporting demand for premium 
retail and mixed-use destinations.
Expansion of Organised Retail
India’s retail market is shifting towards organised formats, creating long-term opportunities 
for high-quality malls and integrated retail environments with strong tenant curation and 
consumer engagement.
Growth in Experience-led Consumption
Consumers are increasingly preferring destinations that combine shopping, dining, 
entertainment, hospitality and leisure, supporting higher footfall, longer dwell time and 
stronger consumption density.
Expansion of Grade A Office Demand
Growth in Global Capability Centres (GCCs), technology firms and flexible workspace 
operators is driving demand for premium office developments integrated with social and retail 
infrastructure.
Urban Infrastructure and Connectivity
Investments in metro connectivity, roads, airports and urban infrastructure are 
improving accessibility and expanding consumption catchments around existing and 
upcoming developments.
Macroeconomic Slowdown
Inflationary pressures, weaker consumer sentiment or moderation in economic growth could 
impact discretionary spending and retail consumption trends.
Geopolitical Uncertainty
Volatility in energy prices, trade conditions and global financial markets may impact inflation, 
borrowing costs and investment activity.
Increasing Competition
Rising supply across retail, office and mixed-use developments in key urban markets may 
intensify competition for tenants, occupiers and consumers.Company Overview
About The Phoenix Mills Limited
The Phoenix Mills Limited (PML) is India’s leading 
owner, operator and developer of retail-led mixed-
use destinations. Our integrated model spans the full 
lifecycle: land acquisition, design, development, leasing, 
and long-term operations, enabling us to build and scale 
high-quality, consumption-driven mixed-use assets with 
disciplined capital allocation.
With over 20 million sq. ft. delivered to date and a visible 
pipeline through 2030 and beyond, we are well positioned 
to expand the annuity portfolio while maintaining high 
occupancy, productivity and yield discipline.
Portfolio Overview
Retail
Our retail portfolio today spans 12 experience-driven city 
centre destinations across 8 major cities in India, with a 
gross leasable area of over 11 million sq. ft. Assets include 
Phoenix Palladium (Mumbai), Phoenix MarketCity (Mumbai, 
Bengaluru and Chennai), Phoenix Avenue of Stars, Pune (earlier known as Phoenix MarketCity Pune), Phoenix 
Palassio (Lucknow), Phoenix Pride of India, Indore (earlier 
known as Phoenix Citadel, Indore), Palladium Ahmedabad, 
Phoenix Mall of the Millennium (Pune), Phoenix Mall of Asia 
(Bengaluru) and Phoenix United (Lucknow, Bareilly).
Located in strategic micro-markets, these assets 
function as integrated urban destinations that combine 
retail, dining, entertainment, and leisure. Each asset 
is anchored by a curated mix of global and domestic 
brands aimed at enhancing footfall, dwell time and tenant 
productivity. This combination of location quality, leasing 
capability, and active asset management has enabled 
us to consistently deliver high consumption density and 
resilient rental growth.
Retail Business Performance
During FY26, consumption (retailer sales) reached an all-
time high of ₹16,587 crore, growing 21% YoY. Retail rental 
income grew 10% to ₹2,157 crore, and EBITDA grew 12% 
to ₹2,246 crore. This performance was delivered with no 
new mall additions during the year, and while key assets 
Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore and Phoenix Avenue of 
Stars, Pune were under active repositioning.

Consumption Growth Drivers
Consumption growth during the year was broad-based. 
Phoenix Mall of Asia, was the standout performer, with 
consumption growing by 95% to ₹2,213 crore. It is now 
the second-largest contributor to consumption across the 
portfolio. Phoenix Mall of the Millennium grew 30%, while 
established assets such as Phoenix Palladium Mumbai and 
Phoenix Palassio both grew 16%. The rest of the portfolio 
(excluding the malls under repositioning) delivered healthy 
double-digit growth.
Across categories, discretionary and experience-led 
segments drove momentum. Jewellery grew by 35%, family 
entertainment and multiplexes grew by 22% and fashion 
and accessories grew by 16%. Excluding jewellery and 
electronics, consumption still grew by approximately 15%, 
reflecting healthy underlying everyday demand.

Leasing and Brand Strategy
Leasing momentum was strong in FY26, with around 920 
deals completed covering approximately 3.2 million sq. 
ft. and over 400 new store openings across the portfolio. 
The quality of incoming tenants continued to improve, 
with a balanced mix of global and domestic brands across 
luxury, mass-premium, and lifestyle categories. These 
include Rolex, Golden Goose, Victoria's Secret, Ikea, 
Uniqlo, Bershka, Lego, Onitsuka Tiger, Tanishq, Lifestyle, 
Azorte, Game Palacio, and Pantaloons to name a few. These 
launches have further strengthened our positioning as 
the preferred destination for leading brands entering and 
expanding across India. 
Experience-Led Initiatives
Our experiential strategy operates across three layers: 
permanent destination formats, brand partnership 
activations, and owned programming.
At the foundation, the Gourmet Village at Phoenix 
Palladium, housing around 19 brands across 
approximately 85,000 sq. ft., has scaled into a meaningful 
contributor to both consumption and rentals, while visibly 
driving dwell times and repeat visits. Having validated 
the format, we are now replicating it across multiple 
assets in the portfolio, starting with Phoenix Palassio and 
Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore.
We are also expanding the role of our destinations beyond 
retail. The Phoenix Racquet Club at Phoenix Palladium 
Mumbai is an early example of this; bringing an active 
lifestyle into the mall environment and broadening 
the reasons consumers choose to spend time with us. 
Additionally, we have also added experiences such as a Go 
Karting Rink at Phoenix Pride of India and an Ice Skating 
Arena at Phoenix Mall of the Millennium. 
Brand partnerships have added a premium experiential 
layer across the portfolio. During the year, our festive 
experiences included a Diwali installation created in 
partnership with Armani and a Christmas installation in 
partnership with Sephora, both at Phoenix Palladium. 
These collaborations extended brand engagement beyond 
the store itself. They gave brands more room to create 
experiences while giving customers new reasons to visit 
and interact with the physical space.Our owned in-house IPs, such as Phoenix Shopping 
Festival, Holiday Land, Food Festivals, and Christmas at 
Phoenix, anchor the year-round engagement rhythm. The 
calendar also features live concerts, cultural showcases, 
children’s workshops, and community festivals. Together, 
these drive consistent footfall across age groups and 
visitation occasions.*
* Refer to the Intellectual Capital chapter in this Integrated Annual 
Report for more details.

COMMERCIAL OFFICES
Our Grade A commercial offices form a critical component 
of our integrated platform, providing a second stable 
economic driver alongside retail. By embedding offices 
within retail-led destinations, we target corporate 
occupiers who value proximity to premium amenities, 
retai l, and dining. 
The portfolio today comprises seven Grade A 
developments across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, and 
Chennai, with a combined GLA of around 4.8 million sq. 
ft. Occupiers include corporate head offices, new-age 
businesses, and global capability centres, all categories 
with strong demand for high-quality and amenity-
integra ted workplaces.
New Launches
Our office portfolio has grown from nearly 2 million sq. ft. 
as of March 2024 to around 4.8 million sq. ft. as of March 
2026. During 2025, we launched three offices, Phoenix 
Asia Towers (Bengaluru), Millennium Towers (Pune) and 
One National Park (Chennai).

to fund our pipeline and broader growth agenda.

a calibrated manner, with upcoming projects 
concentrated in Bengaluru and Kolkata, markets 
where we have established presence or identified high-
